assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 individual character monograph series/lycoris-recoil/03 V2 Working Artifacts/05 Specialist Synthesis/LYCORIS_RECOIL_ERIKA_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md (20,971 bytes, status canonical, empty supersession arrays, do_not_use_as_current_authority false), a portrait of the DA Lycoris Janome Erika, the hostage Takina's E01 shot freed, in the Japanese TV series and the Friends Shorts. Its load-bearing scenes are E01, E03, E11-E13 and Short 06, located by episode, cue, timecode, retained still and the project's claim and visual IDs; it reads E03 C0339 through the owner's 23 November listening return and the E11 briefing and Short 06 exterior movement through the attributed audiovisual returns. Its author inspected the cited Japanese subtitles and sampled stills but did not hear her performance or watch the sequence continuously. The section 'Three ways other tellers put her among people' (Recollect V01 and V02, Asaura's Gluttony days and the React contributor story) is an attributed print comparison outside the television continuity, and no prediction here rests on it. The readings, ledgers, baseline and reconciliation records it links are not curated on this subject, and no claim rests on them directly. The discovery row does not claim speech or ethics. The project's COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY outcome was not adopted as a grade. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Her history belongs to her at every state, so far as the portrait gives it, which is little: her years of service, exact age and a full account of her capture are undisclosed. Located present states: held at gunpoint and calling 'Go ahead and shoot' before Takina fires (E01); calling 'Wait, Takina!' as Takina leaves headquarters, arguing with Hibana over the word 'avenge', conceding the failed capture, rising at the rumor of Takina's return and admitting she could not think what to say (E03); no private settlement with Takina through E04-E10; welcoming Takina at the briefing, then 'Fuki, let her go' with the offer to fill Takina's position, followed, after Sakura's accusation, by 'all my fault' and a direct apology (E11 10:15-11:11), the located point at which the conversation she wanted finally happens; leading the evacuation with Hibana, 'I have to take Takina's place', and receiving Takina's thanks, saying she should have spoken to the commander and answering 'You really are awful' (E12); tending Sakura's wound, challenging Fuki about the wounded and offering to go with Takina (E13). Short 06 is placed as the portrait places it, without a calendar. Nothing after E13; print stories are outside scope.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The portrait's closing section draws a limited expectation from located differences: with Hibana and without Takina she names an injustice and concedes the weak point in her argument (E03); with Takina present the approach is hard until she has something concrete to do (E03, E11); with Fuki in charge she proposes, protests and holds on while Fuki decides (E11, E13, Short 06); with Sakura hurt she turns to the need in front of her (E13). It predicts that she corrects an account of Takina's rescue as harm to her, considers offering to take up a teammate's task, and may receive an answer she dislikes from whoever decides. It predicts overreach: 'all my fault' goes beyond anything she could establish about headquarters' decision (E11). Not B: the portrait says whether having a useful act to offer generally helps her speak 'one especially well-observed instance cannot answer'; in E13 she wants both to stay with Sakura and to go with Takina, and Fuki, not she, decides; and a private conversation without a practical opening, an unfamiliar civilian's claim on her, and a conflict between DA policy and her own future have much less evidence behind them. What decides her own choice when her wishes conflict and no superior decides is not established, which is insufficiency, not productive uncertainty. The portrait keeps her E11 motive open between repaying Takina and helping two partners reach each other, but that does not change which act is predicted. Not D: each pattern is located across E03, E11-E13 and Short 06.

Located states: captive (E01); defending the absent Takina and unable to speak to her (E03); no private settlement through E04-E10; the offer and apology at E11 10:15-11:11, the located point at which the conversation happens; carrying out the offer and accepting an unflattering judgment from Takina while still trailing off (E12); practical care and a refused offer (E13). The portrait locates the change in what passes between Erika and Takina, and shows her repeating the E03 words in a new direction. Not B: it locates no change in her disposition, and does not establish how often she tried to speak in E04-E10. Not D: the states are located by episode, cue and timecode.

Located forms: あたし heard by the owner at her first overlap with Hibana (E03 C0339); the broken-off concession そうだけど…そうなんだけど！ (E03, repeated to Takina in E12); 'Fuki, let her go' with the familiar name and 私がたきなのポジション埋めますから (E11); 「あのときはホントにごめんなさい」 (E11); the near-verbless 「お泊りは！」 (Short 06); short urgent calls ('Wait, Takina!', 'Then I'll go too!') and practical instructions to the wounded Sakura (E13). The discovery row does not claim speech. Not B: the portrait says her self-reference near E03 16:32.7 remains a listening question and makes no claim about pitch or a vocal reading of 私, and its author did not hear her performance continuously. Not D: several Japanese forms are located and contrasted by addressee.

Located in one ordinary scene only: offering the proverb that gossip lasts seventy-five days, laughing at Sakura's absence with regret Chisato doubts, and gripping her chair to ask about the sleepover before Fuki sends them home (Short 06). The café visit and the squirrel dessert in print are outside scope. Not D: a single scene gives no repeated habit.

Directed differences, stated by the portrait and located: Hibana (critic, confidante and tease, with whom Erika can be angry, hopeful and embarrassed in one afternoon, E03, E12); Takina (the rescuer she defends in absence and cannot approach until she has something to offer, then apologizes to and lets judge her, E03, E11, E12); Fuki (the person whose permission counts, to whom she proposes, protests and clings, and whose refusals stand, E11, E13, Short 06); Sakura (who blames her in E11 and explains her debt in E12, and whom she tends without a prior reconciliation, E13). Not A: the Takina approach rests on one practical opening, and no private conversation between them is shown. Not C: each relationship has located acts and a stated difference.

Located self-reports: she could not think what to say to Takina (E03); she has wanted to talk to her (E11); it was all her fault (E11); she should have spoken properly to the commander (E12); she wants the sleepover (Short 06). The portrait keeps her E11 motive open between repayment and helping two partners, leaves her expectation in the E01 seconds outside the scene, and says Chisato's teasing does not decide what moved her laugh in Short 06. Not B: no settled motive is stated for her central acts. Not D: her own statements about difficulty and fault are located.

Located modes with outcomes: arguing over 'avenge' with Hibana and conceding the failed capture (E03); proposing to Fuki that Takina be let go (E11); accepting Sakura's accusation and going further (E11); answering back when Takina calls her awful, and staying (E12); challenging Fuki about the wounded and offering to go, refused (E13); gripping the chair for the sleepover, refused (Short 06). Not B: each mode is observed once or twice, and the portrait says conflict with an unfamiliar civilian or with DA policy has much less evidence. Not D: the modes are located and differ by addressee.

Located positions: asking the people outside her captor's grasp to intervene, a request the portrait says is finite in scope (E01); defending the rescue from her own survival while conceding that someone the team should have captured died (E03); taking the blame and saying she should have spoken to the commander (E12); challenging Fuki about the wounded girl (E13). The row does not claim ethics, and the portrait says a conflict between DA policy and her own future has much less evidence. Not C: the E03 concession is broken off, and she is not shown reasoning a choice through. Not E: her positions are located in her own words.

Located only as reactions: laughing at Sakura's absence with regret Chisato calls unconvincing (Short 06); answering back to Takina's 'You really are awful' (E12); responding at once when Hibana pretends to spot Takina (E03). Not D: no play of her own initiative is sustained.

One dedicated portrait locates its load-bearing scenes (E01, E03, E11-E13, Short 06) by cue, timecode, still and claim ID and relies on attributed audiovisual returns where voices compete. Not B: the row curates only this derived item; its author did not hear her performance or watch the sequence continuously; and about a quarter of the text is print comparison outside the continuity. Not D: every scene it relies on is located.

Located bounds against overreading: her E01 request does not select Takina, prescribe the means, decide what happens to the dealers or release Fuki from the standby order, and her willingness to face danger is poor evidence of indifference to her life; the E11 briefing allows both her address and Takina's alarm to be genuine; 'all my fault' exceeds what she could establish about the decision, and no published DA rule says one girl had to be dismissed for the other to stay, which is Sakura's reckoning; her use of 'partner' leaves Takina's relationship with Chisato intact (E12); her E13 offer does not place her beside Takina; Short 06's exterior movement does not settle where she went; and E04-E10 do not establish how often she tried to speak. Not A: no forecast about her is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.

Television states are placed by episode, cue and timecode, and the E11 offer and apology are located within the scene. Not B: there is no story calendar, her service history is undisclosed, and Short 06 is not placed in the episode sequence. Not D: the episode states are precisely located.

conditions: Illustrative lines only, in the located forms: urgent appeals and offers to Fuki using her given name ('Fuki, let her go', 私がたきなのポジション埋めますから, 'Then I'll go too!'), a direct apology for 'back then', the broken-off concession そうだけど…そうなんだけど！, a near-verbless demand like 「お泊りは！」, and practical instructions to a wounded teammate (E03, E11-E13, Short 06).

Excluded: extended or private conversation with Takina, a settled self-reference (あたし is heard once and the pronoun near E03 16:32.7 is a listening question), and any claim about pitch or vocal reading.
scenario_readiness.note: The discovery row does not claim speech. The located forms constrain short illustrative lines in the sampled situations only.

conditions: Someone describes Takina's rescue of her as harm to her: predict that she corrects the account from her own survival, and concedes a strong objection about the mission when it is put to her, possibly trailing off (E03; the closing section).
A teammate must leave work that someone else can take up: predict that she considers offering to take it, addressed to whoever holds the decision (E11, E12; the closing section).
Blamed for her old failure: predict that she accepts the blame, possibly beyond what she can establish, and apologizes directly to the person affected (E11, E12).
A proposal refused by Fuki: predict protest or holding on, then Fuki's decision stands (E13, Short 06).
A wounded teammate in front of her: predict direct practical care without a reconciliation first (E13).
Include her overreach: blame beyond what she knows, and offering more than one course at once (E11, E13).

Exclude: a private conversation with Takina without a practical opening, an unfamiliar civilian's claim on her, a conflict between DA policy and her own future, and any choice she must make herself without a superior deciding.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Television E01-E13, with Short 06 placed without a calendar. From E01 to the E11 offer (10:15-11:11) she has not managed to speak with Takina; from that offer onward the apology has been made, and in E12 Takina thanks her. Nothing after E13.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Takina as the rescuer she owes, Hibana as teammate and confidante, Fuki as field leader, Sakura as a peer who blames her and is wounded in E13, and Chisato. A comparable new teammate or superior is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: DA headquarters and field operations, and the café, in the series' Tokyo.
No print scene, no private or domestic setting, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow extrapolation follows the portrait's closing section. Her own choice when her wishes conflict and no superior decides is not established, so it is excluded.
One café scene (Short 06) gives her wish to stay and a refused request; ordinary social life beyond it would be invented.
Her positions are located but not reasoned through, the row does not claim ethics, and the portrait says a conflict between DA policy and her own future has much less evidence.
The television evidence gives her no romantic interest or choice; the denial of being in love in Recollect is print and outside scope.

conditions: Team work under Fuki: filling a vacated position, leading the evacuation of the wounded with Hibana, rejoining the fight, and tending a wound (E11-E13).
Excluded: field command, her training and service history, and dealings with DA command.
scenario_readiness.note: Her team work under Fuki in E11-E13 is the best-located part of the portrait.

known_limits.statement: Whether having a useful act to offer generally helps her speak rests on one well-observed instance (E11), which the portrait says cannot answer it.
Her E11 offer may be repayment, help for two partners, or both; only the order of the exchange, the offer volunteered before anyone pressed her, is firm.

'All my fault' goes beyond anything she could establish about headquarters' decision; no published DA rule says one girl had to be dismissed for the other to stay, which is Sakura's reckoning (E11-E12).

Her E01 request does not select Takina, prescribe the means or release Fuki from the standby order, and her willingness to face danger is poor evidence of indifference to her life; her expectation in those seconds is outside the scene.
In E13 she wants to stay with the wounded Sakura and to go with Takina; Fuki refuses her offer, so her own choice between them is not shown.

あたし is heard by the owner at E03 C0339, but the pronoun near E03 16:32.7 remains a listening question; the portrait makes no claim about pitch or a vocal reading of 私, and its author did not hear her performance continuously.
E04-E10 offer no private settlement with Takina and do not establish how often she tried to speak.
Her years of service, exact age and a full account of her capture are undisclosed.
The Recollect, Gluttony days and React scenes are attributed comparisons outside the television continuity and are not used for prediction.
Untested: a private conversation without a practical opening, an unfamiliar civilian's claim on her, and a conflict between DA policy and her own future.
Her ordinary life is sampled in one café scene.
